claims.text: The record cannot establish that the rider was anywhere other than inside Terminal 3. The rider leg of the trace holds 88 fixes and every one of them reports 45 m to 80 m horizontal accuracy, so every one falls outside the 25 m accuracy filter that POL-NS-02 applies to driver fixes and that POL-NS-04(c) applies symmetrically to rider fixes; rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. The 2,039 m minimum and 2,101 m mean distance those raw fixes report from the pickup pin are therefore inadmissible readings rather than evidence that the rider was away: under POL-NS-04(c) rider fixes below the accuracy filter 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence', and a rider track whose every fix is filtered out is undecidable and expressly neutral, not adverse. I accept that POL-NS-04 does not otherwise apply here, because limb (a) requires a coordinating message from the rider and the chat log contains none; but the neutrality rule its limb (c) states is what governs this rider track, and on that rule the rider's account that he was in the terminal is neither contradicted nor confirmed by the trace.

Nothing on this record shows the rider was ever reached. The chat log holds three messages and no more — the system arrival notice at 23:13:11, MSG-00202-002 at 23:14:02 and MSG-00202-003 at 23:19:30 — and all three, the platform's own notice included, carry read_at null; the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, so the driver never used the voice channel that POL-NS-04(b) treats as the alternative to a chat reply. I disclose that the chat log is impaired: issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85, and I rely on it only for what it establishes despite that discount — that the driver's two 'still waiting' texts and the platform's arrival notification were never acknowledged by anyone, and that he cancelled roughly ten minutes after arriving without trying any channel other than unread in-app text. That is the disclosure POL-GEN-02(1) requires of me, and the artifact's own admissibility note records that its content is consistent with the rider's account rather than against it.

Neither party's profile can carry this case against the rider, and I name the only fields that may be used. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3-or-more trigger in POL-NS-09(d), and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so POL-NS-09(c) cannot fire on this record. rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is 1 and the driver's is 0, but those are lifetime counters: they are not the trailing-30-day field POL-NS-09(d) reads, and under POL-GEN-01 reading the lifetime counter where the clause names the trailing-window counter is the commonest way an adverse finding gets built on reputation, and a claim that does it is discarded. I disclose that the driver profile artifact is impaired — SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, weight 0.9 — and I cite it only for the two zero counter-party dispute figures and the counters that sit an order of magnitude below the POL-NS-07 thresholds.

If the case is to turn on whether this rider should bear the fee at all, that question is not settled by the record and the answer the policy gives is escalation rather than collection. Rider presence is the only fact that speaks to the rider's side of the no-show test, and the only artifact that touches it is the trace, whose rider leg is filtered out in its entirety; POL-NS-04(c) says in terms that this leaves the artifact impaired for the purposes of POL-NS-08(b), and where the sole evidence for a fact is impaired under limb (b) the matter escalates under POL-NS-09 instead of being resolved against the party it disfavours. I again disclose that the chat artifact I cite to show the rider was never reached is impaired (UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85, per POL-GEN-02(1)). Escalation is terminal and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded while the reviewer settles the open question: whether a rider who was inside Terminal 3, whose arrival notice was never read and whom the driver never telephoned, should be charged a no-show fee on a trace that cannot place him at all.

I do not press the two arithmetic routes that are closed to the rider, and I do not ask the judge to stretch them. The derived dwell is a single continuous qualifying run of 620 seconds — 63 fixes from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05 inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius — against the 480 second AIRPORT minimum, a surplus of 140 seconds (shortfall_sec -140.0), so no waiting-period shortfall argument under POL-NS-06 is available; and the same derived facts put the driver in-radius and holding position 25 seconds before he tapped 'arrived' at 23:13:10, so no false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 is available either. The rider's case rests on the points above, not on those.

claims.text: Limb (a) of the chargeable-no-show test is met on the face of the record: the trip record for TRP-00202 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-24T23:13:10+08:00, and the trip is recorded as cancelled by the driver, not abandoned before arrival.

Limb (b) is met: the driver's GPS trace has him inside the AIRPORT arrival radius of 150 m at and before the arrival event — the qualifying in-geofence run opens at 23:12:45, a full 25 seconds before the 23:13:10 arrival marker, and the trace's closest approach to the pin is 22.4 m, far inside the 150 m radius the fee schedule sets for the Changi kerbside.

Limb (c) is met with room to spare: the driver held position inside the geofence in a single unbroken qualifying run of 63 GPS fixes lasting 620 seconds, from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05. That clears the 480-second AIRPORT minimum by 140 seconds; the shortfall field reads -140.0, i.e. a surplus, and limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival tap, which is exactly how this run is computed.

Limb (d) is met: the trip record shows no boarding event and records the trip terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW at 23:23:20 — fifteen seconds AFTER the required 480-second dwell elapsed at 23:23:05, so the cancellation falls at or after the moment the dwell was complete as limb (d) requires. The reason code is one of the three limb (d) recognises, and this is not a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE case that would divert the matter to POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 does not defeat the fee, because the arrival marker is not false. At 23:13:10 the driver was already stationary inside the 150 m radius — the dwell had opened 25 seconds earlier — so he was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at or above the 15 km/h motion threshold at the moment the marker was set. The clause's own limb (iii) confirms a marker set by a driver who then genuinely waits the full period does not void an otherwise good fee.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Limb (a) requires a rider chat message that locates or coordinates, and the chat log contains only the system 'driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages — there is no rider message at all, so limb (a) fails before limb (b) or (c) is reached. Limb (c) would in any event be undecidable rather than satisfied: every one of the rider's 88 fixes reports 45 m to 80 m horizontal accuracy and is filtered out, leaving rider_qualifying_fix_count at 0, which POL-NS-04 expressly makes neutral rather than adverse.

POL-NS-06's premature-cancellation refund is not triggered: the effective in-geofence dwell of 620 seconds exceeds the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, so there is no shortfall to refund. Because the plain dwell already suffices, the driver does not need the limb (i) advisory-accumulation route, and the MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00202-01 — which carries weight 0.0 — is immaterial to the outcome either way. That absence is citable but nothing turns on it here.

No limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged, so nothing is impaired for policy purposes. There is no clock skew: the 23:13:10 arrival marker coincides with a GPS fix on the trace's 10-second cadence. There is no trace defect: 116 fixes, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0. The chat log holds exactly the 3 messages trip_record.chat_message_count records. And the fare reconciles: the $6.00 cancellation fee equals the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), which is the figure POL-NS-08(d) requires.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 entitles the driver to compensation of 80 percent of the $6.00 cancellation fee, i.e. SGD 4.80. The anti-farming check does not bite, and it requires BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 168 is 0.006, far below the 0.08 rate test. These are the only two profile fields POL-NS-07 permits to be read.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires. The deciding facts rest on unimpaired artifacts (GPS trace and trip record both at weight 1.0), so limb (e) is not reached; the parties' counterparty-dispute counters are both 0, so limb (c) is not reached; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3 in limb (d). The case is decidable and should be ruled, not escalated.

The ruling this record supports is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, not NO_ACTION. POL-NS-07 pays the driver, and under POL-GEN-03 the emitted ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 4.80, while the filing rider's own charge stands as it presently is. The driver's counterparty statement — that he waited past ten minutes at Door 5 and lost the airport queue — is corroborated by the trace, not merely asserted.

Two artifacts on this bundle carry pre-pass impairment and the driver discloses both, per POL-GEN-02: the chat log EV-CHAT-00202 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue UNREAD_MESSAGE, and the driver profile EV-DPROF-00202 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.9 with issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH. Neither carries the deciding fact — the dwell and the cancellation reason are carried by the GPS trace and trip record at full weight — and both are down-weighted in confidence only; the findings above survive the discount. The driver's case does not depend on either.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: the SGD 6.00 no-show fee is not refunded, and the reason is the policy's four-part test in POL-NS-01, which this record satisfies on all four limbs. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 23:13:10. (b) The GPS trace (weight 1.0, 116 fixes, zero gaps, 100% coverage) puts the driver inside the 150 m Changi Terminal 3 arrival radius from 23:12:45 — 25 seconds before the 'arrived' tap — with a closest approach of 22.4 m. (c) He held station there in a single unbroken qualifying run of 63 fixes lasting 620 seconds, against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, a surplus of 140 seconds. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 23:23:20 as RIDER_NO_SHOW, 15 seconds after the required dwell elapsed, with no boarding event. Your two arithmetic arguments are correct and I accept them: POL-NS-05 does not help you (the marker was not false — the driver was already stationary in-radius when he tapped it) and POL-NS-06 does not help you (there is no dwell shortfall to refund). Your point that the rider leg of the trace is undecidable is also correct: all 88 rider fixes report 45–80 m accuracy and are filtered out, so the trace neither places you in the terminal nor proves you away from it, and I treat it as neutral rather than adverse. But rider presence is not what decides this fee: POL-NS-01 nowhere requires the rider to have been present, and the clause that would have used your presence, POL-NS-04, does not apply because its limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from you in the chat log, and the log contains no rider message at all. For the same reason I reject the argument that the case must escalate on the rider track: POL-NS-09(e) escalates only where the deciding fact is carried solely by an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d), and here the deciding facts — arrival, dwell and termination — are carried by the GPS trace and the trip record at full weight. I accept that neither you nor the platform's arrival notice read the driver's two texts (all read_at null, and trip_record.in_app_calls empty), which is why an in-app message was not a reasonable way to reach you; but an unread message does not defeat a fee the driver otherwise earned, and the chat impairment goes to weight, not to the outcome. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 6.00 Changi Airport no-show fee stands, and the driver is entitled to compensation of SGD 4.80.

The facts. The driver accepted the job at 23:04, reached T3 Arrival Door 5, and his GPS trace places him inside the 150 m airport arrival radius from 23:12:45, holding position in one unbroken run of 63 fixes for 620 seconds until 23:23:05 — 140 seconds longer than the 480 seconds an airport pickup requires, measured (as POL-NS-01(c) requires) from the first in-geofence fix and not from his 23:13:10 'arrived' tap. He cancelled at 23:23:20 for RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the waiting period had run, and the trip record shows no boarding event. All four conditions of POL-NS-01 are therefore met, and none of POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces them: the driver was inside the arrival radius (so POL-NS-03, wrong-entrance, does not apply), the marker was set while he was already stationary inside the geofence (so POL-NS-05, false marker, does not apply), and the dwell exceeded the minimum (so POL-NS-06, shortfall, does not apply).

To the rider: I accept that the GPS cannot show where you were — all 88 of your fixes report 45 m to 80 m accuracy and fall below the 25 m filter, so under POL-NS-04(c) they are neutral, evidence of neither presence nor absence, and the 2,039 m/2,101 m distances those raw fixes report are inadmissible readings, not proof you were away. But rider presence is not a condition of the fee, and POL-NS-06 states in terms that the fee stands whether or not the rider was present or responded. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you because its limb (a) requires a coordinating message from you and the chat log contains none — only the platform's arrival notice and two driver messages, so limb (a) fails before limb (b) or (c) is reached. Your escalation argument also fails: POL-NS-09(e) requires the deciding fact to rest solely on evidence impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), and here the deciding facts (arrival and dwell) rest on the GPS trace and trip record, both at full weight 1.0. The rider track is present rather than omitted and no clause under consideration relies on rider position, so POL-NS-08(b) is not engaged; nor do POL-NS-09(c) or (d) fire, since the counterparty-dispute counters are both 0 and no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below the threshold of 3). Nor can either profile carry a finding against you: POL-GEN-01 makes rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counters context only, and the only citable profile fields read in your favour.

To the driver: under POL-NS-07 you are paid 80% of the SGD 6.00 fee — SGD 4.80 — with the platform retaining the residual SGD 1.20 as its service fee. The anti-farming check does not bite: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (the threshold is 4 or more) and the rate against 168 completed trips in 30 days is 0.006 (the threshold is above 0.08). Two artifacts on the bundle are impaired and I name them, their weights and their issue codes as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: the chat log EV-CHAT-00202 at weight 0.85 (issue UNREAD_MESSAGE) and the driver profile EV-DPROF-00202 at weight 0.9 (issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH). Neither carries the deciding facts — arrival and dwell come from the full-weight GPS trace and trip record — so the profile's 0.9, read only for the anti-farming figures, caps confidence at 0.9, above the 0.70 floor, and the findings survive the discount. Because the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, the amount this ruling moves is the SGD 4.80 compensation figure; your SGD 6.00 charge stands, and the payment to the driver is made separately and is never netted against it. No clause produces a referral on these facts.
